description: The 3D modelling commands beyond the primitives and Boolean operations already catalogued: procedural and NURBS surface creation and editing (network, blend, patch, offset, fillet, trim, extend, sculpt, control vertices), conversions between solids, surfaces, NURBS and meshes, the subdivision mesh toolset (smoothing, refining, creasing, face extrusion, split/merge/collapse/spin/cap), solid utilities (thicken, offset edge, extract edges, interference), 3D transforms (array, mirror, scale), the section-object commands and the system variables that govern history, defining-geometry deletion, display tessellation and surface associativity.

tools.name: PLANESURF
tools.description: Creates a planar surface either as a rectangle from two diagonal corners or from one or more closed, coplanar objects (polylines, circles, regions, splines). It is the usual starting face for trimming, offsetting or PRESSPULL and the quickest way to cap a planar opening. The result is a procedural surface whose U/V isolines follow SURFU/SURFV.
tools.usage:
PLANESURF
Specify first corner or [Object] <Object>: <point> | O
Specify other corner: <point>
Object: Select objects: <closed planar objects> Enter

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Each closed object becomes its own surface; islands are not subtracted (use SURFTRIM afterwards).

parameters.name: SURFU / SURFV
parameters.description: Number of isolines displayed in each direction on new surfaces (0-200, default 6).

parameters.name: DELOBJ
parameters.description: Whether the source objects are deleted after conversion.

tools.example:
PLANESURF
O
(select the closed floor outline) Enter
THICKEN (select the surface) 200
tools.notes: Surfaces created from the corners prompt lie on the current UCS XY plane. Non-planar or open objects are rejected; use SURFPATCH or EXTRUDE for those.

tools.name: SURFNETWORK
tools.description: Creates a surface through a network of curves or surface edges in two directions (like LOFT with guides in both U and V): select the curves running one way, then the curves running the other way, and the surface is fitted to all of them. Used for hulls, car bodies and any free-form face bounded by sketched sections. Continuity with adjacent surfaces is set per edge (G0/G1/G2) with a bulge magnitude.
tools.usage:
SURFNETWORK
Select curves or surface edges in first direction: <selection> Enter
Select curves or surface edges in second direction: <selection> Enter
(if surface edges were selected) Press Enter to accept or [CONtinuity/Bulge magnitude]:

parameters.name: first / second direction
parameters.description: Splines, lines, arcs, polylines, elliptical arcs or existing surface/solid edges; curves in one direction need not touch each other but must cross the other set.

parameters.name: CONtinuity
parameters.description: G0 (position), G1 (tangent) or G2 (curvature) where the network attaches to existing surface edges.

parameters.name: Bulge magnitude
parameters.description: 0-1, how strongly the surface bulges away from the edge for G1/G2.

parameters.name: SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY
parameters.description: 1 keeps the surface linked to its defining curves so editing a curve rebuilds the surface.

tools.example:
SURFNETWORK
(select the three cross-section splines) Enter
(select the two longitudinal splines) Enter
tools.notes: A procedural (associative) surface is created when SURFACEMODELINGMODE is 0; set it to 1 for a NURBS surface with editable control vertices. Gaps between curves larger than the modelling tolerance cause 'unable to create network surface'.

tools.name: SURFBLEND
tools.description: Creates a transition surface between the edges of two existing surfaces or solids, with G0, G1 (tangent) or G2 (curvature-continuous) continuity at each side and an adjustable bulge. It is the 3D counterpart of BLEND and the way to join two surface panels smoothly; with CHain a whole loop of connected edges is picked at once.
tools.usage:
SURFBLEND
Continuity = G1 - tangent, bulge magnitude = 0.5
Select first surface edges to blend or [CHain]: <edges> Enter
Select second surface edges to blend or [CHain]: <edges> Enter
Press Enter to accept the blend surface or [CONtinuity/Bulge magnitude]:

parameters.name: CHain
parameters.description: Select all contiguous edges at once.

parameters.name: CONtinuity
parameters.description: Set G0/G1/G2 for the first and second edge sets independently.

parameters.name: Bulge magnitude
parameters.description: 0-1 per side (default 0.5); larger values give a rounder transition.

tools.example:
SURFBLEND
CH
(pick an edge of the upper panel) Enter
CH
(pick an edge of the lower panel) Enter
CON
G2
G2
tools.notes: Grips on the result let the continuity and bulge be changed later when SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY is on. The two edge sets must not intersect.

tools.name: SURFPATCH
tools.description: Closes an opening bounded by surface edges or by a closed loop of curves with a new surface, optionally constrained by guide curves and with tangent or curvature continuity to the surrounding surfaces. It caps holes in surface models before SURFSCULPT or THICKEN turns them into solids.
tools.usage:
SURFPATCH
Continuity = G0 - position, bulge magnitude = 0.5
Select surface edges to patch or [CHain/CUrves] <Select>: <edges> Enter | CH | CU
Press Enter to accept the patch surface or [CONtinuity/Bulge magnitude/Guides]:

parameters.name: CUrves
parameters.description: Patch a closed loop of curves (spline, polyline) instead of surface edges.

parameters.name: Guides
parameters.description: Additional curves the patch must pass through, shaping its interior.

parameters.name: CONtinuity / Bulge magnitude
parameters.description: As SURFBLEND, applied to all boundary edges.

tools.example:
SURFPATCH
CH
(pick an edge of the hole) Enter
CON
G1
tools.notes: The loop must be closed and planar-ish; highly twisted loops fail or produce folds - add guides. After patching, SURFSCULPT can convert the closed shell to a solid.

tools.name: SURFOFFSET
tools.description: Creates a parallel copy of a surface (or region) at a given distance, in one direction, both directions, or as a solid whose thickness is the offset; the Connect option keeps multiple offset surfaces joined at their shared edges. Arrows preview the offset direction and Flip reverses it. This is how shells, wall thicknesses and clearance surfaces are made from a modelled face.
tools.usage:
SURFOFFSET
Connect adjacent edges = No
Select surfaces or regions to offset: <selection> Enter
Specify offset distance or [Flip direction/Both sides/Solid/Connect/Expression] <0>: <distance> | F | B | S | C | E

parameters.name: Flip direction
parameters.description: Reverse the offset side shown by the arrows.

parameters.name: Both sides
parameters.description: Create two surfaces, one on each side.

parameters.name: Solid
parameters.description: Produce a 3D solid between the original and the offset (like THICKEN).

parameters.name: Connect
parameters.description: Keep the offsets of several connected surfaces joined.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: Type a formula or a parameter name for the distance (parametric).

tools.example:
SURFOFFSET
(select the hull surface) Enter
S
8
tools.notes: Offsetting inward by more than the smallest radius of curvature fails (self-intersection). Associative offsets follow the source surface when SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY is 1.

tools.name: SURFFILLET
tools.description: Creates a constant-radius fillet surface between two surfaces or regions, trimming both to the fillet by default. Pick the two surfaces on the sides where the fillet should lie; the radius can be changed before accepting and the trim behaviour turned off to keep the originals whole.
tools.usage:
SURFFILLET
Radius = 1.0, Trim Surface = yes
Select first surface or region to fillet or [Radius/Trim surface]: <pick> | R | T
Select second surface or region to fillet or [Radius/Trim surface]: <pick>
Press Enter to accept the fillet surface or [Radius/Trim surfaces]:

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Fillet radius; must be smaller than the surfaces allow.

parameters.name: Trim surface
parameters.description: Yes trims both surfaces to the fillet; No leaves them intact.

tools.example:
SURFFILLET
R
5
(pick the top face)
(pick the side face)
tools.notes: For solids use FILLETEDGE instead. The fillet is a procedural surface with a radius grip when associativity is on.

tools.name: SURFTRIM
tools.description: Trims portions of a surface where it meets other surfaces, regions or curves projected onto it: choose the surfaces to trim, the cutting objects, then click the areas to remove. Cutting curves are projected along the current UCS Z, the view direction or none (must lie on the surface). SURFUNTRIM restores trimmed areas by selecting the trimmed edge or the surface.
tools.usage:
SURFTRIM
Extend surfaces = Yes, Projection = Automatic
Select surfaces or regions to trim or [Extend/PROjection direction]: <selection> Enter
Select cutting curves, surfaces, or regions: <selection> Enter
Select area to trim [Undo]: <click the part to remove> Enter
SURFUNTRIM
Select edges on surface to un-trim or [SURface]: <edge> | SUR then pick the surface

parameters.name: Extend
parameters.description: Yes extends the cutting surfaces to fully cross the trimmed surface.

parameters.name: PROjection direction
parameters.description: Automatic, View, UCS or None - how curves are projected onto the surface.

parameters.name: SURFACEAUTOTRIM
parameters.description: 1 makes PROJECTGEOMETRY trim the surface automatically.

tools.example:
CIRCLE (drawn above the surface)
SURFTRIM
(select the surface) Enter
(select the circle) Enter
(click inside the projected circle) Enter
tools.notes: Trimmed surfaces keep their untrimmed definition, which is why SURFUNTRIM can recover them and why CVREBUILD has a 'retrim' option. Regions and solids cannot be trimmed with this command (use SLICE / SUBTRACT).

tools.name: SURFEXTEND
tools.description: Lengthens a surface by a distance from selected edges, either continuing the surface's own shape (Extend) or stretching it straight (Stretch), and either merging the extension into the original surface or appending a separate surface. Used to make surfaces overrun before trimming so that SURFTRIM and SLICE have something to cut against.
tools.usage:
SURFEXTEND
Modes = Extend, Creation = Append
Select surface edges to extend: <edges> Enter
Specify extend distance [Expression/Modes]: <distance> | E | M
Modes: Extension mode [Extend/Stretch] <Extend>:  Creation type [Merge/Append] <Append>:

parameters.name: Extend
parameters.description: The extension follows the curvature of the surface.

parameters.name: Stretch
parameters.description: The extension is tangent-linear from the edge.

parameters.name: Merge / Append
parameters.description: One larger surface, or the extension as a new surface object.

tools.example:
SURFEXTEND
(pick the outer edge of the roof surface) Enter
M
S
M
300
tools.notes: Extending a trimmed edge is not allowed; untrim first. NURBS surfaces can only be extended with Merge.

tools.name: SURFSCULPT
tools.description: Converts a set of surfaces (and/or solids) that together enclose a watertight volume into a single 3D solid, trimming away the parts of the surfaces outside the enclosed region. It is the final step of surface modelling - after the shell is closed with SURFPATCH/SURFBLEND, SURFSCULPT produces the solid that can be booleaned, shelled and mass-analysed.
tools.usage:
SURFSCULPT
Select surfaces or solids to sculpt into a solid: <selection> Enter
tools.example:
SURFSCULPT
(select the six surfaces of the housing) Enter
-> a single 3D solid; the surfaces are consumed
tools.notes: Fails with 'the surfaces do not form a closed volume' when there are gaps larger than the modelling tolerance; SURFEXTEND the offending surfaces so they overlap and try again. Surfaces with G0 joints work, but the solid keeps sharp edges.

tools.name: SURFEXTRACTCURVE
tools.description: Creates curves on a surface, solid face or region: isolines in the U or V direction at picked points, a chain of isolines, or a spline through picked points on the surface. The extracted curves are ordinary splines/lines that can be used as paths for SWEEP, boundaries for SURFTRIM or references for dimensions.
tools.usage:
SURFEXTRACTCURVE
Select a surface, solid, or face: <pick>
Select point on surface or [Chain/Direction/Spline points]: <point> | C | D | S
Direction: [U/V]

parameters.name: Chain
parameters.description: Extract the isoline across all adjacent surfaces.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: Toggle between U and V isolines.

parameters.name: Spline points
parameters.description: Pick points on the surface to draw a spline lying on it.

tools.example:
SURFEXTRACTCURVE
(pick the wing surface)
D
V
(click at three positions along the wing) Enter
tools.notes: Introduced in 2013. Curves are not associative to the surface. For projecting existing 2D geometry onto a surface use PROJECTGEOMETRY.

tools.name: PROJECTGEOMETRY
tools.description: Projects points, lines, arcs, polylines, splines and other curves onto a surface, solid or region along the UCS Z axis, the view direction or a picked vector, creating new curves that lie on the target. When SURFACEAUTOTRIM is 1 the target surface is trimmed by the projection at the same time - the way logos, cut-outs and part lines are wrapped onto curved faces.
tools.usage:
PROJECTGEOMETRY
Select curves, points to be projected or [PROjection direction]: <selection> | PRO
Select a solid, surface, or region for the target of the projection: <pick>
PROjection direction: [UCS/View/Vector] <UCS>:  (Vector: specify two points)

parameters.name: UCS
parameters.description: Project along the current UCS Z axis (default).

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: Project along the current viewing direction.

parameters.name: Vector
parameters.description: Project along a direction given by two points.

parameters.name: SURFACEAUTOTRIM
parameters.description: 1 trims the target surface with the projected curves automatically.

tools.example:
SURFACEAUTOTRIM 1
PROJECTGEOMETRY
(select the slot polyline drawn above the panel) Enter
(pick the curved panel)
-> the slot is cut out of the panel
tools.notes: Projected curves onto solids are created but the solid is not trimmed (use the curves with IMPRINT or SLICE). Text must be exploded to curves (TXTEXP) before projection.

tools.name: CVADD
tools.description: Adds control vertices to a NURBS surface or spline at a picked location (or by inserting knots), giving finer local control for subsequent editing with 3DEDITBAR or grips; CVREMOVE takes control vertices away to simplify the shape. On surfaces the new row of CVs runs in the U or V direction chosen with the Direction option.
tools.usage:
CVADD
Select a NURBS surface or curve to add control vertices: <pick>
Select point on surface [Insert Knots/Direction]: <point> | I | D
CVREMOVE
Select a NURBS surface or curve to remove control vertices: <pick>
Select point on surface [Direction]: <point>

parameters.name: Insert Knots
parameters.description: Add knots (and therefore CVs) without changing the shape.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: U or V row for surfaces.

tools.example:
CONVTONURBS (select the loft surface)
CVSHOW (select it)
CVADD (pick it, click near the middle, Direction U)
tools.notes: Only NURBS objects: convert procedural surfaces first with CONVTONURBS. Adding CVs to a degree-3 surface keeps the shape; removing CVs changes it.

tools.name: CVREBUILD
tools.description: Rebuilds a NURBS surface or spline with a new number of control vertices and degree in U and V through the Rebuild Surface/Curve dialog, which also reports the maximum deviation from the original. Rebuilding with fewer, evenly spaced CVs gives cleaner shapes that are easier to edit; trimmed surfaces can be retrimmed automatically after the rebuild.
tools.usage:
CVREBUILD
Select a NURBS surface or curve to rebuild: <pick>
(Rebuild Surface dialog: Control Vertices Count U/V, Degree U/V, Options: Delete input geometry, Retrim previously trimmed surface; Maximum Deviation readout; Preview)

parameters.name: Control Vertices Count
parameters.description: Number of CVs in each direction (minimum degree+1).

parameters.name: Degree
parameters.description: 1-11 per direction; 3 is the usual choice.

parameters.name: Retrim previously trimmed surface
parameters.description: Reapply the trims after rebuilding.

parameters.name: Maximum Deviation
parameters.description: Read-only distance between the new and old surface - increase CVs if it is too large.

tools.example:
CVREBUILD
(pick the surface; U 8, V 6, degree 3/3, Delete input geometry, OK)
tools.notes: Also works on splines (as SPLINEDIT's rebuild). Rebuilding destroys associativity with defining curves.

tools.name: CVSHOW
tools.description: Displays the control vertices (the CV hull) of selected NURBS surfaces and splines so they can be dragged with grips or edited with 3DEDITBAR; CVHIDE turns them off again. Showing CVs is the entry point to free-form editing - drag a CV to push or pull the surface locally.
tools.usage:
CVSHOW
Select NURBS surfaces or curves to display control vertices: <selection> Enter
CVHIDE  (hides CVs on all objects; no selection)
tools.example:
CVSHOW
(select the NURBS surface) Enter
(drag individual CV grips; use the 3D gizmo to constrain to an axis)
tools.notes: CV display is not saved with the drawing. Procedural surfaces have no CVs; CONVTONURBS them first.

tools.name: 3DEDITBAR
tools.description: Displays an edit bar gizmo on a point of a NURBS surface or spline for reshaping it: drag the point to move the surface locally, drag the tangent handle to change the tangent direction, or set the tangent magnitude, with the base point relocatable. It offers more control than dragging raw control vertices because the surface is pulled through the picked point.
tools.usage:
3DEDITBAR
Select a NURBS surface or curve to edit: <pick>
Select point on NURBS surface: <point>
(gizmo: drag point / tangent handle; right-click options: Move point location, Move tangent direction, Specify tangent magnitude, Relocate base point, Constrain to X/Y/Z axis or plane)

parameters.name: Move point location
parameters.description: Translate the surface point (the CVs around it adjust).

parameters.name: Move tangent direction / magnitude
parameters.description: Change the slope and the influence distance at the point.

parameters.name: Relocate base point
parameters.description: Move the gizmo to another point on the surface.

tools.example:
3DEDITBAR
(pick the hood surface)
(click near the centre; drag the point 20 mm upward along Z)
tools.notes: Editing a NURBS surface this way breaks its link to any defining curves. Use DELOBJ/UNDO if the result must be reverted; the change is one undo step.

tools.name: CONVTOSOLID
tools.description: Converts eligible objects into 3D solids: closed mesh objects (with the smoothing/faceting rule set by SMOOTHMESHCONVERT), surfaces that enclose a volume, closed polylines and circles with thickness, and wide polylines with thickness. It is the route from a sculpted mesh or a closed surface set to a solid that supports Booleans and MASSPROP.
tools.usage:
CONVTOSOLID
Mesh conversion set to: Smooth and optimized.
Select objects: <selection> Enter
SMOOTHMESHCONVERT = 0 smooth+optimized (merge coplanar faces) | 1 smooth, not optimized | 2 faceted+optimized | 3 faceted, not optimized

parameters.name: meshes
parameters.description: Must be closed (no holes); MESHCAP holes first.

parameters.name: surfaces
parameters.description: A set of surfaces fully enclosing a volume (like SURFSCULPT).

parameters.name: polylines / circles with thickness
parameters.description: Closed, uniform-width polylines and circles that have a non-zero Thickness property become extruded solids.

parameters.name: SMOOTHMESHCONVERT
parameters.description: Smooth (rounded NURBS-like faces) or Faceted (planar faces per mesh face), optimized (coplanar faces merged) or not.

tools.example:
SMOOTHMESHCONVERT 0
CONVTOSOLID
(select the smoothed mesh) Enter
tools.notes: Meshes with self-intersections or non-manifold edges are refused. Converting a heavily subdivided mesh with SMOOTHMESHCONVERT 3 creates thousands of faces and slow solids; smooth conversion is usually preferable. The MESHOPTIONS dialog exposes the same settings.

tools.name: CONVTOSURFACE
tools.description: Converts objects into surfaces: 2D solids, regions, mesh objects, planar 3D faces, open polylines/lines/arcs with thickness (become extruded surfaces), and 3D solids (each face becomes a surface, the solid is consumed). Used to get editable surfaces from a solid for SURFOFFSET/SURFTRIM work, or to turn legacy thickness geometry into real surfaces.
tools.usage:
CONVTOSURFACE
Mesh conversion set to: Smooth and optimized.
Select objects: <selection> Enter

parameters.name: DELOBJ
parameters.description: Controls whether the source objects are deleted.

parameters.name: SMOOTHMESHCONVERT
parameters.description: As for CONVTOSOLID when the input is a mesh.

tools.example:
CONVTOSURFACE
(select the 3D solid box) Enter
-> six surfaces
ERASE (the unwanted ones)
SURFOFFSET ...
tools.notes: Closed polylines with thickness become surfaces open at top and bottom; use CONVTOSOLID if a solid is wanted. The reverse of converting a solid is SURFSCULPT or CONVTOSOLID on the enclosing surfaces.

tools.name: CONVTONURBS
tools.description: Converts procedural surfaces and 3D solids into NURBS surfaces (each solid face becomes a NURBS surface) so they can be edited with control vertices (CVSHOW, CVADD, 3DEDITBAR, CVREBUILD). Procedural surfaces keep associativity with their defining curves; NURBS surfaces trade that for direct shape control.
tools.usage:
CONVTONURBS
Select objects: <surfaces or solids> Enter

parameters.name: SURFACEMODELINGMODE
parameters.description: 0 creates procedural surfaces from surface commands, 1 creates NURBS directly, avoiding the conversion step.

tools.example:
CONVTONURBS
(select the lofted surface) Enter
CVSHOW (select it) Enter
tools.notes: Conversion is one-way; there is no CONVTOPROCEDURAL. Meshes must first become surfaces (CONVTOSURFACE).

tools.name: CONVTOMESH
tools.description: Converts 3D solids, surfaces, regions, closed polylines, 3D faces, polyface/polygon meshes and legacy meshes into subdivision mesh objects that can be smoothed, creased and sculpted with the MESH* commands. The tessellation density and initial smoothness come from the Mesh Tessellation Options (MESHOPTIONS). MESHSMOOTH does the same conversion.
tools.usage:
CONVTOMESH  (or MESHSMOOTH)
Select objects: <selection> Enter
MESHOPTIONS: Mesh Tessellation Options dialog - mesh type (Smooth mesh optimized / Mostly quads / Triangles), distance from original faces, angle between faces, max edge length, aspect ratio, smoothness after tessellation

parameters.name: Mesh type
parameters.description: Smooth Mesh Optimized adapts face size to curvature; Mostly Quads and Triangle give regular grids.

parameters.name: Smoothness after tessellation
parameters.description: Initial smoothing level 0-4 applied to the converted mesh.

parameters.name: FACETERDEVSURFACE / FACETERMAXEDGELENGTH
parameters.description: System variables behind the dialog's distance and edge-length controls.

tools.example:
MESHOPTIONS (Mostly quads, max edge length 10, smoothness 0)
CONVTOMESH
(select the solid cylinder) Enter
MESHSMOOTHMORE (select it)
tools.notes: Solids with history lose it. Converting large solids with tiny edge lengths creates very heavy meshes. The old MESH primitives (3DMESH, PFACE) are legacy polygon meshes, not subdivision meshes, until converted.

tools.name: MESH
tools.description: Creates subdivision mesh primitives - box, cone, cylinder, pyramid, sphere, wedge, torus - with the same size prompts as the solid primitives, using the tessellation divisions set in MESHPRIMITIVEOPTIONS (e.g. how many faces a box has in each direction) and the initial smoothness level. Mesh primitives are the starting blocks for organic modelling by pushing faces, creasing and smoothing.
tools.usage:
MESH
Current smoothness level is set to : 0
Enter an option [Box/Cone/CYlinder/Pyramid/Sphere/Wedge/Torus/SEttings] <Box>:
(size prompts as BOX/CONE/... e.g. Specify first corner / other corner / height)
MESHPRIMITIVEOPTIONS: Mesh Primitive Options dialog - tessellation divisions per primitive (Length/Width/Height, Axis/Height/Base), preview smoothness

parameters.name: SEttings
parameters.description: Set the smoothness level (0-4) for the primitive being created.

parameters.name: DIVMESHBOXLENGTH / WIDTH / HEIGHT, DIVMESHCYLAXIS / BASE / HEIGHT, DIVMESHSPHEREAXIS / HEIGHT, DIVMESHTORUSPATH / SECTION ...
parameters.description: System variables storing the division counts per primitive type.

parameters.name: SMOOTHMESHMAXLEV / SMOOTHMESHMAXFACE
parameters.description: Maximum smoothing level (default 4) and maximum face count allowed for a mesh.

tools.example:
DIVMESHBOXLENGTH 6
DIVMESHBOXWIDTH 4
DIVMESHBOXHEIGHT 3
MESH
B
0,0,0
60,40
30
MESHSMOOTHMORE (select the box) -> rounded block
tools.notes: Meshes have no volume for MASSPROP; convert with CONVTOSOLID when properties are needed. Sub-object selection (Ctrl+click faces/edges/vertices, or the Filter in the Mesh ribbon) is how individual faces are moved, scaled or extruded.

tools.name: MESHSMOOTHMORE
tools.description: Increases the smoothness level of selected mesh objects by one (up to SMOOTHMESHMAXLEV, default 4), rounding the shape by subdividing the display of each face while keeping the control cage editable; MESHSMOOTHLESS decreases it. Smoothing is a property (Smoothness in the Properties palette), not a geometric change, so it can be undone at any time - unlike MESHREFINE.
tools.usage:
MESHSMOOTHMORE
Select mesh objects to increase the smoothness level: <selection> Enter
MESHSMOOTHLESS
Select mesh objects to decrease the smoothness level: <selection> Enter

parameters.name: Smoothness 0-4
parameters.description: 0 shows the raw faceted cage; each level quadruples the displayed faces.

parameters.name: SMOOTHMESHMAXLEV
parameters.description: Upper limit (1-255, default 4); higher values are slow.

tools.example:
MESHSMOOTHMORE
(select the mesh head) Enter
MESHSMOOTHMORE
(select it again) Enter  -> level 2
tools.notes: Creased edges (MESHCREASE) resist smoothing. Smoothness above 2 is rarely needed before conversion to a solid.

tools.name: MESHREFINE
tools.description: Multiplies the number of editable faces of a mesh object, or of selected faces, by converting the current smoothing level's subdivided faces into real faces of the control cage and resetting the smoothness to 0. Refine when you need finer local control (more faces to push and pull); it is irreversible except by UNDO and makes the mesh heavier.
tools.usage:
MESHREFINE
Select mesh object or face subobjects to refine: <object or Ctrl+click faces> Enter

parameters.name: whole object
parameters.description: All faces are refined; requires smoothness level >= 1.

parameters.name: face subobjects
parameters.description: Only the selected faces are subdivided, keeping the rest coarse.

tools.example:
MESHSMOOTHMORE (select the mesh)
MESHREFINE
(Ctrl+click the four faces around the nose) Enter
tools.notes: Refining a level-0 mesh does nothing; smooth it first. The face count is capped by SMOOTHMESHMAXFACE.

tools.name: MESHCREASE
tools.description: Sharpens selected mesh edges, faces or vertices so they resist smoothing: a crease value of Always keeps the edge perfectly sharp at every smoothness level, while a numeric value keeps it sharp only up to that level and rounds it above. MESHUNCREASE removes the crease. This is how a smooth organic body keeps hard edges at a parting line or a flat base.
tools.usage:
MESHCREASE
Select mesh subobjects to crease: <Ctrl+click edges/faces/vertices> Enter
Specify crease value [Always] <Always>: <0-4 level> | A
MESHUNCREASE
Select crease to remove: <subobjects> Enter

parameters.name: Always
parameters.description: Edge stays sharp regardless of smoothness.

parameters.name: level value
parameters.description: Crease effective up to that smoothing level (e.g. 2: sharp at levels 0-2, smoothed at 3-4).

tools.example:
MESHCREASE
(Ctrl+click the four bottom edges of the box) Enter
A
MESHSMOOTHMORE (the top rounds, the base stays flat)
tools.notes: Creasing a face creases all of its edges. Creases survive CONVTOSOLID as sharp edges when converting smooth.

tools.name: MESHEXTRUDE
tools.description: Extrudes one or more mesh faces outward (or inward with a negative height) to add volume, along the face normal, a direction, a path or with a taper - the mesh equivalent of PRESSPULL. Adjacent extruded faces can be joined into one block or extruded individually, which is set with the Setting option.
tools.usage:
MESHEXTRUDE
Adjacent extruded faces set to: Join
Select mesh face(s) to extrude or [Setting]: <Ctrl+click faces> Enter | S
Specify height of extrusion or [Direction/Path/Taper angle/Expression]: <height>

parameters.name: Setting
parameters.description: Join adjacent faces into one extrusion (Yes) or extrude each face separately (No).

parameters.name: Direction / Path / Taper angle
parameters.description: As EXTRUDE: two points, a path curve, or a draft angle.

tools.example:
MESHEXTRUDE
(Ctrl+click the two side faces) Enter
25
tools.notes: Extruding a face on a smoothed mesh extrudes the underlying cage face. Use MESHSPLIT first to extrude only part of a face.

tools.name: MESHSPLIT
tools.description: Splits one mesh face into two along a line between two picked points on its edges (or vertices), adding topology exactly where it is needed without refining the whole mesh. It is the precise alternative to MESHREFINE for placing an edge loop before extruding or creasing.
tools.usage:
MESHSPLIT
Select a mesh face to split: <click face>
Specify first split point on face edge or [Vertex]: <point on edge> | V
Specify second split point on face edge or [Vertex]: <point on edge> | V

parameters.name: Vertex
parameters.description: Snap the split to an existing vertex instead of a point along an edge.

tools.example:
MESHSPLIT
(click the top face)
(click the midpoint of the left edge)
(click the midpoint of the right edge)
tools.notes: Splitting creates two faces that may be non-planar; smoothing handles that. Splits on triangular faces can produce degenerate faces - prefer MESHSPIN or MESHMERGE to clean up.

tools.name: MESHMERGE
tools.description: Merges two or more adjacent mesh faces into one face, removing the shared edges. Used to simplify topology after splits or refinement, or to make one large flat face before extruding it. The merged face may be non-planar, which shows as a facet crease when smoothing is 0.
tools.usage:
MESHMERGE
Select adjacent mesh faces to merge: <Ctrl+click faces> Enter
tools.example:
MESHMERGE
(Ctrl+click the six small faces on the front) Enter
MESHEXTRUDE (select the merged face) 10
tools.notes: Faces must share edges; disconnected faces are rejected. Merging can create faces with many vertices that CONVTOSOLID handles poorly - keep them roughly planar.

tools.name: MESHCOLLAPSE
tools.description: Collapses a mesh face or edge to a single vertex, pulling the surrounding vertices together and removing the face - the way pinch points, poles and unwanted small faces are eliminated. It is the opposite of MESHSPLIT/MESHREFINE in effect.
tools.usage:
MESHCOLLAPSE
Select mesh face or edge to collapse: <Ctrl+click>
tools.example:
MESHCOLLAPSE
(Ctrl+click the tiny sliver face)
tools.notes: Collapsing on a smoothed mesh can create visible dents; check at smoothness 0. Only one face or edge per command run.

tools.name: MESHSPIN
tools.description: Spins the shared edge of two adjacent triangular mesh faces so it connects the other pair of vertices, changing which diagonal a quad is split along. It corrects the shading and smoothing direction of triangulated regions without adding or removing faces.
tools.usage:
MESHSPIN
Select first triangular mesh face to spin: <click>
Select second adjacent triangular mesh face: <click>
tools.example:
MESHSPIN
(click the two triangles forming the quad on the shoulder)
tools.notes: Both faces must be triangles sharing one edge. Quads should be preferred for smooth subdivision; MESHMERGE two triangles to make one.

tools.name: MESHCAP
tools.description: Creates a new mesh face that closes a hole bounded by a connected loop of mesh edges, making the mesh watertight so CONVTOSOLID can produce a solid. Pick the edges around the opening (Ctrl+click) and the cap face is created; large caps can then be split for better smoothing.
tools.usage:
MESHCAP
Select connecting mesh edges to create a new mesh face: <Ctrl+click the boundary edges> Enter
tools.example:
MESHCAP
(Ctrl+click the four edges around the open top) Enter
CONVTOSOLID (select the mesh) Enter
tools.notes: The edges must form a single closed loop; open or branching selections fail. A cap over a curved opening is non-planar and smooths with the rest.

tools.name: THICKEN
tools.description: Converts a surface into a 3D solid by giving it a thickness, offsetting the surface in the normal direction (negative values go the other way). It is the standard way to turn sheet-like surface models - roofs, shells, sheet-metal panels - into solids for Booleans and mass properties.
tools.usage:
THICKEN
Select surfaces to thicken: <selection> Enter
Specify thickness <0>: <value or negative value>

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Positive along the surface normal, negative against it.

parameters.name: DELOBJ
parameters.description: Whether the source surface is deleted.

tools.example:
THICKEN
(select the curved panel) Enter
-3
tools.notes: Thickening tightly curved surfaces inward beyond their radius fails. For meshes use CONVTOSOLID; for regions use EXTRUDE.

tools.name: OFFSETEDGE
tools.description: Creates a closed polyline (or spline) that is offset inward or outward from the edges of a planar face on a 3D solid or surface, with sharp or rounded corners. The resulting curve lies on the face and is normally used immediately with PRESSPULL or EXTRUDE to create a boss, pocket or rim - the modelling equivalent of a sketch offset in parametric CAD.
tools.usage:
OFFSETEDGE
Corner = Sharp
Select face: <click a planar face>
Specify through point or [Distance/Corner]: <point> | D | C
Distance: Specify distance <n>:  Specify point on side to offset:
Corner: [Sharp/Round]

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: Offset by a value; then click inside or outside the face for the side.

parameters.name: Corner
parameters.description: Sharp keeps mitred corners; Round fillets them with the offset distance.

tools.example:
OFFSETEDGE
D
5
(click the top face)
(click inside the face)
PRESSPULL (click inside the offset polyline) -10
tools.notes: Only planar faces; the face's outer loop is offset, inner loops (holes) are ignored. Introduced in 2013.

tools.name: XEDGES
tools.description: Extracts wireframe geometry - lines, arcs, circles, ellipses, splines - from every edge of selected 3D solids, surfaces, meshes, regions or from sub-object edges (Ctrl+click), leaving the source object intact. It produces the 2D/3D curves needed for wire models, sweep paths, dimension references or export to systems that only accept curves.
tools.usage:
XEDGES
Select objects: <solids/surfaces/meshes or Ctrl+click individual edges> Enter
tools.example:
XEDGES
(Ctrl+click the top circular edge of the cylinder) Enter
-> a CIRCLE object on the current layer
tools.notes: Extracted curves are placed on the current layer and are not associative. For a full 2D projection of a solid use FLATSHOT or the model documentation views (VIEWBASE).

tools.name: INTERFERE
tools.description: Finds where 3D solids (and surfaces, in newer releases) overlap: compares one selection set with another (or all members of one set with each other), highlights each interference, lets you zoom to and step through them, and optionally creates new solids representing the overlapping volumes. It is the clash-check tool for pipework against structure or fit checks of parts.
tools.usage:
INTERFERE
Select first set of objects or [Nested selection/Settings]: <selection> Enter
Select second set of objects or [Nested selection/checK first set] <checK>: <selection> Enter | Enter to check the first set against itself
(Interference Checking dialog: Interfering objects list, Previous/Next, Zoom to pair, Delete interference objects created on Close [checkbox])

parameters.name: Nested selection
parameters.description: Select solids inside blocks and xrefs.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Visual style and colour used to highlight interference, and whether to highlight the pair or the interference solid.

parameters.name: Delete interference objects created on Close
parameters.description: Untick to keep the intersection solids in the drawing (useful for reporting volumes with MASSPROP).

tools.example:
INTERFERE
(select all pipes) Enter
(select the steel beams) Enter
(step through the 3 interferences with Next; untick Delete, Close)
tools.notes: -INTERFERE gives a command-line version for scripts that reports the count only. Meshes must be converted to solids first. Results are not saved as a report; use the created solids or LIST.

tools.name: 3DARRAY
tools.description: Creates a non-associative rectangular array with rows, columns and levels (Z), or a polar array about an axis defined by two points, in 3D. It predates the associative ARRAY (which since 2012 also supports levels), so it is mainly used in scripts and where independent copies are wanted.
tools.usage:
3DARRAY
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Enter the type of array [Rectangular/Polar] <R>:
Rectangular: Enter the number of rows (---) <1>: / columns (|||) <1>: / levels (...) <1>: then Specify the distance between rows / columns / levels
Polar: Enter the number of items in the array: / Specify the angle to fill (+=ccw, -=cw) <360>: / Rotate arrayed objects? [Yes/No] <Y>: / Specify center point of array: / Specify second point on axis of rotation:

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Copies stacked along Z with the given spacing.

parameters.name: axis of rotation
parameters.description: Two points define the polar axis, allowing arrays about any 3D axis.

tools.example:
3DARRAY
(select the bolt) Enter
P
8
360
Y
0,0,0
0,0,1
tools.notes: The associative ARRAYRECT/ARRAYPOLAR with Levels option produce editable arrays and are preferred interactively. 3DARRAY is defined in 3darray.lsp and is not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: MIRROR3D
tools.description: Mirrors objects across an arbitrary plane in 3D, defined by three points, a planar object, the last plane, the Z axis (normal and a point), the current view plane, or the XY/YZ/ZX planes through a point, optionally deleting the source. MIRROR only works in the current UCS plane; MIRROR3D handles symmetric parts and assemblies in any orientation.
tools.usage:
MIRROR3D
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Specify first point of mirror plane (3 points) or [Object/Last/Zaxis/View/XY/YZ/ZX/3points] <3points>:
(define the plane)
Delete source objects? [Yes/No] <N>:

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description: Use the plane of a circle, arc or 2D polyline.

parameters.name: Zaxis
parameters.description: A point on the plane and a point on its normal.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: Plane parallel to the screen through a point.

parameters.name: XY / YZ / ZX
parameters.description: UCS planes through a picked point.

tools.example:
MIRROR3D
(select the bracket half) Enter
YZ
0,0,0
N
tools.notes: MIRRTEXT applies to mirrored text as with MIRROR. The 3D gizmo does not offer mirroring; this command is the only interactive 3D mirror.

tools.name: 3DSCALE
tools.description: Scales 3D objects and sub-objects uniformly, or along one axis or plane of the 3D scale gizmo, about a base point - allowing a solid to be stretched in Z only, which SCALE cannot do. Non-uniform scaling is available for meshes and sub-objects; solids and surfaces can only be scaled uniformly (use SOLIDEDIT/stretch faces or grips for non-uniform edits).
tools.usage:
3DSCALE  (alias 3S)
Select objects: <selection> Enter
Specify base point: <point>
Pick a scale axis or plane: <hover the gizmo and click an axis/plane, or press Enter for uniform>
Specify scale factor or [Copy/Reference]: <factor>

parameters.name: gizmo axis / plane
parameters.description: Constrain the scale to X, Y, Z or XY/YZ/ZX (meshes and sub-objects only).

parameters.name: Copy
parameters.description: Keep the original.

parameters.name: Reference
parameters.description: Scale by a reference length to a new length.

parameters.name: DEFAULTGIZMO
parameters.description: Which gizmo appears when sub-objects are selected: 0 move, 1 rotate, 2 scale, 3 none.

tools.example:
3DSCALE
(Ctrl+click the top face of the mesh box) Enter
(pick its centre)
(click the Z axis of the gizmo)
0.5
tools.notes: Requires a 3D visual style or the 3D Modeling workspace for the gizmo to appear. In 2D Wireframe the command still works with keyboard input.

tools.name: SECTIONPLANEJOG
tools.description: Adds a 90-degree jog to an existing section object's cutting line, turning a straight section into a stepped one that passes through several features (like an offset section in a drawing). Pick the section plane and a point on its line; the jog segment can then be moved with grips.
tools.usage:
SECTIONPLANEJOG
Select section object: <pick the section line>
Specify a point on the section line to add jog: <point>
tools.example:
SECTIONPLANE (draw through the housing)
SECTIONPLANEJOG
(pick the section line)
(click where it should step)
(drag the new segment grip to pass through the second bore)
tools.notes: Jogs are visible in the live section and in 2D sections generated with SECTIONPLANETOBLOCK. Jogged section lines also work with the model documentation VIEWSECTION Offset type, which is generally the better route for drawings.

tools.name: SECTIONPLANETOBLOCK
tools.description: Generates a 2D section/elevation or a 3D section from a section object and saves it as a block (inserted into the drawing, replacing an existing block, or exported to a DWG file), using the appearance settings for boundary, fill, background lines and cut-away geometry from SECTIONPLANESETTINGS. It is the pre-2013 way to derive 2D sections from solids; VIEWSECTION now does this associatively on layouts.
tools.usage:
SECTIONPLANETOBLOCK
(Generate Section/Elevation dialog: Select section plane; 2D Section/Elevation or 3D Section; Source Geometry: Include all objects / Select objects to include; Destination: Insert as new block / Replace existing block / Export to a file; Section Settings...; Create)
then -INSERT-style prompts for insertion point, scale and rotation

parameters.name: 2D Section / Elevation
parameters.description: Flat block with hatched cut fill and background lines.

parameters.name: 3D Section
parameters.description: Solids cut at the plane, as a block.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: New block in the drawing, update an existing one (re-generation after model changes), or a separate DWG.

tools.example:
SECTIONPLANETOBLOCK
(pick the section plane; 2D Section; Include all objects; Insert as new block; Create)
(place at 0,0 scale 1 rotation 0)
tools.notes: The block is static; run the command again with Replace existing block after model changes. Section settings (hatch pattern, line colours) are stored with the section object.

tools.name: LIVESECTION
tools.description: Toggles live sectioning for a section object: when on, the 3D solids, surfaces, meshes and point clouds on one side of the section plane are hidden (or shown faded as cut-away geometry) so the interior is visible in the modelling view, in real time as the plane is dragged. It is a display state, not a modification of the objects.
tools.usage:
LIVESECTION
Select section object: <pick>  (toggles on/off)
Section object grips: flip direction, move plane, change type (Plane/Slice/Boundary/Volume)

parameters.name: Section types
parameters.description: Plane (infinite plane), Slice (plane with thickness), Boundary (finite rectangle), Volume (box) - set with the section object's menu grip.

parameters.name: SECTIONOFFSETINC / SECTIONTHICKNESSINC
parameters.description: Increment values for the offset and thickness spinners of the section object (SECTIONSPINNERS dialog).

tools.example:
SECTIONPLANE
(draw the plane)
LIVESECTION
(pick it) -> the model is cut open
(drag the plane grip to explore)
tools.notes: Only one section object can be live at a time. Live section affects rendering and hidden-line views but not plots of 2D layouts unless the viewport shows the 3D view. Turn it off before FLATSHOT.

tools.name: SECTIONPLANESETTINGS
tools.description: Opens the Section Settings dialog for a section object, controlling how 2D sections, 3D sections and live sections are displayed: intersection boundary (colour, layer, linetype), intersection fill (hatch pattern, scale, colour), background lines (show/hide, hidden lines), cut-away geometry (show, colour, fade %), curve tangency lines, and whether these settings apply to all section objects. These settings feed SECTIONPLANETOBLOCK output.
tools.usage:
SECTIONPLANESETTINGS
Select section object: <pick>
(Section Settings dialog: radio buttons 2D section/elevation block creation settings, 3D section block creation settings, Live Section settings; property grid per element; Activate live section; Apply settings to all section objects; Reset)

parameters.name: Intersection Fill
parameters.description: Show / Face Hatch pattern (e.g. ANSI31) / scale / angle / colour / layer.

parameters.name: Background Lines
parameters.description: Show, and whether hidden lines behind the cut are drawn.

parameters.name: Cut-away Geometry
parameters.description: For live sections: show the removed half faded with a given colour and transparency.

parameters.name: Apply settings to all section objects
parameters.description: Make the dialog values the default for every section plane in the drawing.

tools.example:
SECTIONPLANESETTINGS
(pick the section; 2D section settings: Intersection Fill hatch ANSI31 scale 2 colour 8; Background Lines hidden lines No; OK)
tools.notes: The same dialog is reached from the section object's Properties. Settings are stored per section object in the drawing.

tools.name: SOLIDHIST
tools.description: System variable controlling whether composite 3D solids record their history - the original primitives and Boolean operations - so that the components can be selected (Ctrl+click) and edited later with the changes propagating through the Boolean tree. SHOWHIST decides whether that history is displayed. History makes solids editable after the fact but increases file size and can slow complex models.
tools.usage:
SOLIDHIST = 0 (no history, default since 2013) | 1 (record history for new solids)
SHOWHIST = 0 never show history | 1 per-object Show History property | 2 show history of all solids
Per-object: Properties palette > Solid History > History (Record/None), Show History (Yes/No)
BREP command: removes history from selected solids permanently

parameters.name: History = Record
parameters.description: Booleans keep the operands; Ctrl+click selects an original primitive to move/resize it, and the composite updates.

parameters.name: BREP
parameters.description: Command that strips the history (converts to a plain boundary-representation solid).

tools.example:
SOLIDHIST 1
BOX 0,0,0 100,50 30
CYLINDER 50,25,0 10 30
SUBTRACT (box) (cylinder)
SHOWHIST 2
(Ctrl+click the cylinder inside the box, drag its radius grip)
tools.notes: Solids from EXTRUDE/REVOLVE/LOFT/SWEEP also record their profile as history when SOLIDHIST is 1. Converting to mesh, slicing with a surface or running SOLIDEDIT may remove history.

tools.name: DELOBJ
tools.description: Controls whether the geometry used to create 3D objects (profiles, paths, guides, cross sections) is deleted or retained after EXTRUDE, REVOLVE, SWEEP, LOFT, PRESSPULL, PLANESURF, CONVTO*, THICKEN and similar commands, or whether the user is prompted. Batch modelling scripts set it explicitly so the result is predictable; surface-modelling workflows usually keep the curves (0) so associative surfaces can be edited.
tools.usage:
DELOBJ = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | -1 | -2 | -3
 0  retain all defining geometry
 1  delete profile curves only (LOFT cross sections deleted, paths and guides kept)
 2  delete all defining geometry including paths and guides
 3  (default) delete all defining geometry, and also the source objects of conversion commands
-1  prompt whether to delete profile curves
-2  prompt whether to delete all defining geometry
-3  prompt for all defining geometry including conversion sources

parameters.description: Keep everything - required for editing associative surfaces through their curves.
Clean result, nothing left behind (default).

parameters.name: negative values
parameters.description: Interactive prompt after each command; avoid in scripts.

tools.example:
; script: keep the profiles for later reuse
DELOBJ 0
EXTRUDE (select profile) 50
DELOBJ 3
tools.notes: Registry setting (user), not per drawing. Independent of SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY, but associativity is lost if the defining curves are deleted.

tools.name: DISPSILH
tools.description: Controls the display of silhouette edges of 3D solids and surfaces in the 2D Wireframe visual style (1 on, 0 off) and, together with ISOLINES (number of tessellation lines per curved face, default 4) and FACETRES (smoothness of curved faces in hidden, shaded and rendered views and in STL export, 0.01-10, default 0.5), determines how curved solids look and how heavy their display is. DISPSILHBLOCKS (2022.1) extends the silhouette setting to solids inside blocks.
tools.usage:
DISPSILH = 0 | 1
ISOLINES = 0..2047 (default 4)
FACETRES = 0.01..10.0 (default 0.5)
FACETRATIO = 0 | 1 (aspect ratio of faceting on cylindrical/conic solids)
DISPSILHBLOCKS = 0 | 1

parameters.name: DISPSILH 1
parameters.description: Curved solids show their outline in 2D wireframe and HIDE suppresses the mesh lines; slower regen.

parameters.name: ISOLINES
parameters.description: More lines make curved faces readable in wireframe; 0 shows edges only.

parameters.name: FACETRES
parameters.description: Higher values give smoother HIDE/SHADE/plot and finer STL files; 10 is very slow.

tools.example:
; nicer wireframe for a presentation, then back to defaults
DISPSILH 1
ISOLINES 12
REGEN
; before STL export
FACETRES 8
STLOUT
tools.notes: All three are saved in the drawing and require REGEN to take effect. FACETRES also affects hidden-line plots of curved solids; 0.5 can look polygonal at large scales.

tools.name: SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY
tools.description: Controls whether surfaces created by the SURF*, EXTRUDE, LOFT, REVOLVE, SWEEP, PLANESURF and similar commands stay associated with their defining curves and with each other (1, default) so that editing a curve or a parent surface rebuilds the dependent surfaces; 0 creates independent surfaces. SURFACEMODELINGMODE chooses procedural (0) versus NURBS (1) output, and SURFACEAUTOTRIM decides whether PROJECTGEOMETRY trims automatically.
tools.usage:
SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY = 0 | 1
SURFACEMODELINGMODE = 0 (procedural surfaces) | 1 (NURBS surfaces)
SURFACEAUTOTRIM = 0 | 1
SURFACEASSOCIATIVITYDRAG = 0 no preview while dragging dependent geometry | 1 preview | 2 preview limited to the dragged objects (performance)

parameters.name: SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY 1
parameters.description: Surfaces show a chain-link icon in Properties (Maintain associativity); DELOBJ must keep the curves for this to be useful.

parameters.name: SURFACEMODELINGMODE 1
parameters.description: New surfaces are NURBS with control vertices, never associative.

parameters.name: Properties > Maintain associativity = Remove
parameters.description: Breaks the link for one surface.

tools.example:
SURFACEASSOCIATIVITY 1
DELOBJ 0
LOFT (select three splines) -> associative surface
(grip-edit one spline; the loft updates)
tools.notes: Associative surfaces are heavier and can slow editing of large models; set SURFACEASSOCIATIVITYDRAG 2 or turn associativity off for production geometry. Booleans and SLICE remove associativity.
